items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Tyler sat on the bench outside the principal's office. He stared at his shoes. Down the hall, he could hear his teacher's voice.

Illustration: Tyler sits hunched on a wooden bench outside a door labeled 'Principal.' His backpack is on the floor beside him. His face is turned down and his hands are clasped together in his lap.

What does the illustration help you infer about why Tyler might be there?
items.answer: The illustration suggests Tyler is in trouble or worried. His hunched posture, downcast face, and clasped hands show anxiety. Sitting outside the principal's office with these nervous signals suggests he may have done something wrong and is waiting to face a consequence.

steps: Read the text: Tyler is outside the principal's office, staring at his shoes.
Study the illustration: hunched body, clasped hands, downcast face — all signs of anxiety or guilt.
Combine the clues: the setting (principal's office) plus the body language suggests Tyler is in trouble.
This is an inference because the text does not say he is in trouble — you must use both the words and the picture to figure it out.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Emma had practiced her piano song every day for a month. Now she stood before the audience and took a deep breath.

Illustration: Emma stands at a piano on a stage. The seats in front of her are packed with people. A spotlight shines on her. Her back is straight and her chin is up, but her hands are gripping the edge of the piano bench.

What two things does the illustration show about Emma at the same time? Explain both.
items.answer: The illustration shows that Emma is both confident and nervous at the same time. Her straight back and raised chin show confidence and readiness, while her tight grip on the bench shows she is also nervous. These two details together reveal that Emma has mixed feelings about performing.

steps: Look for more than one detail in the illustration.
Identify what each detail suggests: straight back and raised chin = confidence; gripping the bench = nervousness.
The text supports this by saying she practiced hard (confidence) but also that she took a deep breath (nervousness).
A good inference uses multiple clues from both the illustration and the text.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marcus found a stray kitten behind the school. He carried it inside his jacket so no one would see.

Illustration: Marcus walks down a school hallway. His jacket is zipped up and has an unusual lump in the front. A tiny striped tail pokes out from the bottom of the zipper. Marcus looks sideways at a teacher who is walking past.

What does the illustration tell you about what Marcus is doing and why he might be nervous?
items.answer: The illustration shows Marcus is secretly hiding the kitten in his jacket. The lump and the tiny tail poking out confirm the kitten is inside. His sideways glance at the teacher shows he is nervous about being caught, because he knows sneaking an animal into school is against the rules.

steps: The text says Marcus hid the kitten in his jacket so no one would see.
The illustration adds visual proof: the lump in the jacket and the tail peeking out.
The glance toward the teacher is a key detail — it shows Marcus knows he might get in trouble.
Combining these clues tells us Marcus is sneaking the kitten inside and is worried about being caught.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Lila and her mom stood at the door of an old house. The key in Mom's hand was brand new and shiny.

Illustration: Lila and her mom stand at the front door of a house. The door is open partway. Inside, you can see empty rooms and bare walls. The yard has a real estate sign with 'SOLD' stamped across it. Lila is peering inside with curious eyes.

What does the illustration suggest is happening in this story?
items.answer: The illustration suggests that Lila and her mom are moving into a new home. The 'SOLD' sign on the real estate sign, the new key, and the empty rooms inside all point to a family just buying and moving into a house for the first time.

steps: Read the text: new shiny key, standing at the door of an old house.
Look at the illustration: 'SOLD' sign, empty rooms, bare walls.
A new key plus a sold sign plus empty rooms equals a family moving in.
Lila peering inside curiously also shows this is her first time seeing the inside of this house.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Devon did not want to eat his dinner. 'Just three more bites,' said Dad. Devon crossed his arms.

Illustration: Devon sits at a dinner table with a plate of broccoli and fish in front of him. He has his arms crossed and his face is scrunched up. Dad leans forward from across the table, pointing at the plate. Devon is looking away from the food.

What does the illustration tell you about the conflict in this story?
items.answer: The illustration shows a conflict between Devon and his dad over food. Devon does not want to eat his dinner — shown by his crossed arms, scrunched face, and the way he looks away from the food. His dad is leaning in and pointing at the plate, showing he is pushing Devon to eat. The illustration makes the tension between them clear.

steps: Conflict means a problem or disagreement in a story.
The text shows a conflict: Devon does not want to eat and Dad says 'three more bites.'
The illustration adds to this: Devon's body language (arms crossed, face scrunched, looking away) shows refusal.
Dad leaning forward and pointing shows he is firm. These details together show the conflict clearly.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

On the last day of school, Mrs. Chen stood at the classroom door. She gave each student something as they left.

Illustration: Mrs. Chen stands at an open door. She is handing a small wrapped gift to a student. On the classroom wall behind her, student artwork hangs, and a banner reads 'Have a Great Summer!' A stack of similar wrapped gifts sits on a table next to her.

What does the illustration tell you about Mrs. Chen as a character?
items.answer: The illustration shows that Mrs. Chen is a caring and generous teacher. She has prepared individual wrapped gifts for every student, which takes time and thoughtfulness. The summer banner also shows she celebrates her students. Together, these details paint her as a kind and dedicated teacher.

steps: Read the text: Mrs. Chen gives each student something as they leave on the last day.
Look at the illustration: wrapped gifts, a stack ready for all students, a summer banner, student artwork on the walls.
Think about what these details say about her character — someone who prepares gifts for all students cares about them.
Illustrations can tell us about a character's personality through their actions and their surroundings.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nick and his grandfather walked along the beach. Grandfather pointed at something far away in the water.

Illustration: An older man and a small boy stand on a sandy beach. The man is crouching down to the boy's level and pointing toward the horizon. Far out on the water, a large dark shape breaks the surface. Both figures look in the same direction. The boy's mouth is open in amazement.

What does the illustration suggest that Grandfather and Nick might be looking at?
items.answer: The illustration suggests they might be looking at a whale or large sea creature. The large dark shape breaking the surface of the water is a classic sign of a whale. Nick's open mouth shows amazement, which makes sense if they are seeing something rare and exciting like a whale.

steps: The text says Grandfather pointed at something in the water but does not name it.
Look at the illustration: a large dark shape breaks the water's surface far out to sea.
Nick's amazed expression suggests this is something rare or exciting.
While we cannot be 100% certain, the visual clues strongly suggest a large sea animal such as a whale.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Alicia had been working on her painting for weeks. She finally put down her brush.

Illustration: Alicia stands back from a large canvas on an easel. The painting on the canvas shows a bright sunset over mountains. Alicia's hands and apron are covered with many colors of paint. She is looking at the painting with a small smile and her head tilted to one side.

What does the illustration tell you about Alicia's feelings at this moment?
items.answer: The illustration shows Alicia feels satisfied and maybe a little proud of her work. Her small smile and tilted head suggest she is studying the painting thoughtfully and is pleased with how it turned out. The weeks of work mentioned in the text make this moment of completion feel meaningful.

steps: Read the text: Alicia worked for weeks and finally finished.
Study the illustration: small smile, head tilted, stepping back to look.
Stepping back and tilting your head to look at something you made is a sign of satisfaction.
The weeks of effort in the text make her quiet pride in the illustration make sense.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

The neighborhood kids decided to clean up the empty lot on Maple Street. They worked all Saturday morning.

Illustration: A group of five children are in an overgrown empty lot. Two are pulling weeds, one is picking up trash with gloves on, and two are raking leaves into a pile. Trash bags are lined up along the sidewalk, some already full. The children look focused and busy.

What does the illustration add to the story about what the children accomplished?
items.answer: The illustration shows the specific work the children did: pulling weeds, picking up trash, and raking leaves. Several trash bags are already full, showing they have already made progress. The text says they cleaned up the lot, but the illustration shows the actual tasks they did and how much they got done.

steps: The text only says the kids cleaned up the lot — it is vague.
The illustration gives specific details: weeding, trash pickup, raking, full bags.
The full bags are an important detail — they show real progress has been made.
The illustration brings the vague 'cleaned up' into a concrete, vivid picture of the work.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

When Zoe got home from school, everything was different. She stopped in the doorway and looked around.

Illustration: Zoe stands at the door of a room that has been decorated with colorful streamers and balloons. A banner reads 'Happy Birthday Zoe!' Friends and family are gathered around, some jumping up from behind furniture with their arms raised. Zoe's eyes are wide and her hands cover her mouth.

What does the illustration tell you about what happened when Zoe arrived home?
items.answer: The illustration shows that Zoe is having a surprise birthday party. The decorations, the banner with her name, and the people jumping out from hiding all reveal this is a surprise. Zoe's wide eyes and covered mouth show she was truly surprised. The text hints something is different, and the illustration reveals exactly what it is.

steps: The text creates mystery: 'everything was different' — this is a hint something unusual is happening.
The illustration reveals the answer: a surprise party with decorations, a banner, and people jumping out.
Zoe's reaction (wide eyes, hands over mouth) confirms she did not expect this.
The illustration resolves the mystery the text created.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Oliver sat at the top of the big hill with his sled. He looked down. He swallowed hard.

Illustration: Oliver sits on a red sled at the very top of a steep snowy hill. The hill drops down sharply below him. At the bottom, other children are laughing and pulling their sleds back up. Oliver is gripping the sled's rope tightly, and his eyes are wide.

What does the illustration tell you about how Oliver feels and what he is about to do?
items.answer: The illustration shows that Oliver is about to go down the hill on his sled but is afraid. The steep drop, his tight grip on the rope, and his wide eyes all signal fear. He is hesitating at the top. The text confirms this — 'swallowed hard' is a phrase that shows nervousness. He will sled down, but he is scared to start.

steps: Read the text: Oliver is at the top of a hill with a sled and 'swallowed hard' — a clue he is nervous.
Look at the illustration: steep hill, tight grip on rope, wide eyes at the top.
Other children at the bottom enjoying themselves contrasts with Oliver's fear.
'Swallowed hard' combined with his body language in the illustration tells us he is scared but about to go.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Penny and her dad built something in the backyard all weekend. On Monday, her friends came over to see it.

Illustration: Three children crowd around a wooden structure in a backyard. It is a treehouse built into a large oak tree. It has a small door, a window, and a rope ladder hanging down. Penny stands proudly at the top of the rope ladder, hands on her hips.

What does Penny's pose in the illustration tell you about how she feels?
items.answer: Penny's pose — standing at the top with her hands on her hips — shows she feels proud and confident. She worked on the treehouse all weekend and is now showing it off to her friends. Her posture communicates pride and ownership over what she helped build.

steps: Focus on Penny's specific body language: hands on hips, standing at the top.
Hands on hips at the top of something you built is a classic pose of pride.
The text says she and her dad built it all weekend, which supports the idea that she worked hard on it.
Showing it to friends adds to the proud moment — she wants them to see her accomplishment.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

The old woman knocked on each door on the street. No one answered.

Illustration: An elderly woman stands at a door holding a pie wrapped in a cloth. The house number is 14. Down the street, several other houses have their curtains drawn. The woman's face shows a kind but slightly sad expression.

What does the illustration suggest about the old woman and her situation?
items.answer: The illustration suggests the old woman is trying to be friendly by bringing a pie to a neighbor, but no one is home — or no one is answering. Her kind but slightly sad expression shows she hoped to connect with someone. The drawn curtains on nearby houses suggest the neighborhood may not be very welcoming, which makes her effort feel touching.

steps: The text says she knocked on each door and no one answered.
The illustration adds that she is carrying a pie — a kind gesture of friendship or welcome.
The drawn curtains suggest other neighbors may be avoiding her or simply not home.
Her expression (kind but sad) shows she is disappointed but means well.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

For three days, the twins argued about who would get the top bunk. Finally, Dad sat them both down.

Illustration: Two boys who look alike sit on opposite ends of a bed, arms crossed, frowning at each other. Between them sits Dad, calmly holding a coin in his hand. Dad is looking at both boys with a patient smile.

What does the illustration suggest Dad is about to do to solve the problem?
items.answer: The illustration suggests Dad is about to flip a coin to decide who gets the top bunk. Holding a coin while sitting between two arguing children is a classic way to resolve a disagreement fairly. His calm smile shows he has found a simple, fair solution.

steps: The text says the boys argued for three days and Dad sat them down.
Look at the key detail in the illustration: Dad is holding a coin.
A coin held between two people in a disagreement usually means a coin flip is coming.
Dad's calm, patient smile shows he is confident this will resolve the argument fairly.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

On the morning of the big game, Cleo woke up and looked out her window. Her stomach dropped.

Illustration: Cleo stands at her bedroom window. Outside, the sky is dark gray and rain is pouring down. A soccer ball and cleats sit on the floor next to her bed. Cleo's face falls and she holds the curtain open with one hand.

What do the illustration and the phrase 'her stomach dropped' together tell you about Cleo's situation?
items.answer: Together they tell us that Cleo is disappointed because it is raining on the day of her big soccer game. 'Her stomach dropped' means she felt a sudden rush of disappointment or dread. The illustration shows the rain, her soccer equipment ready to go, and her fallen expression — all confirming that the weather is ruining her big day.

steps: The text gives a feeling clue: 'stomach dropped' means sudden disappointment.
The illustration shows rain, gray sky, and Cleo's sad expression at the window.
The soccer ball and cleats next to her bed confirm she was planning to play.
All clues combined: Cleo was ready for the game, but the rain is a problem that may cancel it.
